final.title: When AI answers drift, narrow the workflow
final.body:
If you run a one-person business, the problem is usually not that AI is “bad.” It is that the workflow is too open. You ask for an answer, and the model reaches for whatever sounds plausible instead of staying inside your process. That is a control problem.

The practical question is simple: can this task be bounded by material you already trust? Your own documents, past answers, rules, or procedures are the right test. If the answer is yes, a grounded workflow can retrieve from approved company material before it answers. In plain English, it looks in your files first instead of wandering the open web.

That does not make hallucinations impossible. It just narrows the room they can happen in, which is the part you can actually manage.

So ask yourself: “Do I have a pile of answers, documents, or procedures I already trust, and am I asking the AI to answer only from that pile?” If yes, the next step is a small pilot inside your own environment, using your own data and tools, with finished code and accounts kept in your name. The timing should be treated as scope, not a promise.

If the answer is no, or you are unsure, keep the task manual for now. Hiring may be the cleaner move when the work needs judgment the model should not improvise around. Even a sharp tool should not be asked to guess its way through accounting.
